title: Speed-up docker builds in CI
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently, the slowest part of CI checks is docker builds - it takes about 30 minutes to complete.
That sometimes slows the process of development, cause we need to wait long time even if only a small feature changed.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Try to apply some of the known techniques to speedup the docker builds:

- caching
- disable `lto = "fat"` for CI builds (not for production)
- ???

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Tried to use `mold` linked in CI, it didn't really help - https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/1811
Maybe the setting was wrong, cause locally it helps a lot.

**Additional context**

It would be ideal if docker builds would take less or equal time to other CI tasks, like integration tests.
Expected minimal improvement is about 30min -> 20min of docker CI tasks

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@reporter 
Just a question regarding mold linker. Did you try putting
```
[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-fuse-ld=/path/to/mold"]
```
for each target in cargo.toml instead of trying to run cargo build through mold -run? Mold -run is a fallback if there is no easy way to specify an alternative linker which is not necessary since rust provides an easy way to do so.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: My two cents, I'm not much familiar with Rust so ignore if it is wrong. I think the docker layer caching is not working. I see you have used cargo-chef to cache. GitHub actions run in a completely new container where the previously cached layer is not present. Therefore, cargo-chef is not able to do its work. Something like this may help. https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/gha/

> My two cents, I'm not much familiar with Rust so ignore if it is wrong. I think the docker layer caching is not working. I see you have used cargo-chef to cache. GitHub actions run in a completely new container where the previously cached layer is not present. Therefore, cargo-chef is not able to do its work. Something like this may help. [docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/gha](https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/backends/gha/)

Cargo chef can be used, the github action(build-push-action per that doc link) in this case is just forwarding the inputs "cacheTo" and "cacheFrom" as ("cache-to" and "cache-from" respectively) args to the buildx command. If you're running the buildx command explicitly in your own action, then you would just make sure to use the appropriate arguments(and the driver type if needed for the type of caching).

> Yeah, this seems to be the case look at this [issue ](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/2644#issuecomment-1500464444) in particular.

Edit: took too long typing my comment -- yeah this issue makes the above alone less useful if you have dependencies that take a while to build. I know there's a couple other Action's I've seen that apparently solve for the reverse scenario.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
Howdy, I used [depot.dev](https://depot.dev/) and was able to get the un-cached build down to around [15 minutes](https://github.com/participant7/qdrant/actions/runs/4894483607/jobs/8738768946) with no Dockerfile changes.
The depot client is a drop-in replacement for the docker client, so no scripts need to change.

I work at depot trying to make builds faster.
Depot provides a hosted buildkit service just like the one used in docker but on native machines with persistent disks.

At my previous start-up we built a rust database with really long build times and spent a lot of time trying to make it fast.  The build time problem we had seems really familiar.

If you are interested in this I'd be happy to open up a PR.
